intro-1.text: Every evening, in Dad's old workshop, a little lamp still turns itself on.

intro-2.text: Hi, we're Hackstreet Boys! And this is Pieces of Home: a cozy adventure about the machines people left on the Moon and Mars!

prob-1.text: Out there, far from home, people left lots of machines behind: mirrors, rovers, landers, even a tiny helicopter!

prob-2.text: Some are still working! Scientists still bounce lasers off the mirrors that Apollo 11 left in nineteen sixty-nine.

prob-3.text: Others went quiet. To most kids, they just look like old junk, very far away. But every one of them has a true story.

prob-4.text: Our challenge is called Abandoned but not Forgotten. It asks: how can we tell the stories of NASA's machines on the Moon and Mars?

sol-1.text: Our answer? A game with a heart! Remi's late dad loved these machines. He built tiny models of their landing sites, and wrote each one a letter.

sol-2.text: Now Remi, alone or with up to three friends, delivers his letters, uncovers each machine's true story, and rebuilds his little robot, Milo, one piece at a time.

sol-3.text: It's free, it plays right in your web browser, and it's made for curious players aged ten and up.

demo-1.text: Let's play! This is the real game. Pull the chain, and the adventure begins!

demo-2.text: Dad's workbench is full of glass domes. Each one holds a model of a real landing site, labeled: model, not to scale.

demo-3.text: Pick the Moon, and whoosh! A little rocket flies you there.

demo-4.text: At Tranquility Base, Remi delivers Dad's letter to the mirrors that Apollo 11 left behind.

demo-5.text: Then a true story card pops up, with a real NASA photo, and every fact links to its source.

demo-6.text: Next, you try the big idea yourself: send a beam of light from Earth to the mirrors, and catch it coming back!

demo-7.text: Bring the part home, and Milo gets brand new eyes! Left behind, still answering.

demo-8.text: On Mars, Opportunity was planned to work for ninety Martian days. It kept going for more than fourteen years! Sometimes the wind blew dust off its solar panels, and gave it more power.

demo-9.text: Ingenuity was planned for up to five test flights. It flew seventy-two times!

demo-10.text: Friends can join with a private room code. No chat, just emotes and kind preset phrases, so it stays safe for kids.

demo-11.text: Dad's notebook keeps everything you discover, with real NASA pictures and their credits.

demo-12.text: And at the very end, Dad's backyard dish turns toward Voyager 1. On November eighteenth, twenty twenty-six, Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object one light-day from Earth.

feat-1.text: Every number in the game comes from a list of checked facts, each with a source link. And every model is clearly labeled.

feat-2.text: There are captions for every line, a printable Field Guide for classrooms, and a calmer motion setting. Even the music is made in code!

data-1.text: And it's built on real NASA data. Photos from the NASA Image and Video Library and Photojournal. A Moon map from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Globe pins at real landing sites. And JPL Horizons data that follows Voyager 1, day by day.

data-2.text: You can even hear real wind on Mars, recorded by the Perseverance rover!

imp-1.text: Pieces of Home helps players see these machines as stories, not junk. Left behind, but still answering. Still teaching. And Voyager 1? Still sending.

imp-2.text: It's free, and ready to play right now, at pieces of home dot pages dot dev. Thanks for watching!

g-2.text: Abandoned but not Forgotten. Some still work today!

g-3.text: This is Pieces of Home. Left behind. Still shining.

g-4.text: Deliver Dad's letters to real machines on the Moon and Mars. Play the science. Rebuild his robot. Every fact and photo, straight from NASA.

g-5.text: Imagine every classroom meeting these machines as friends, not junk.

g-6.text: Play free today, at pieces of home dot pages dot dev!
